# The render contract

What a program outside Tyto can rely on when it asks Tyto to render something (ADR 0011).
**Jacurutu** is the first such program, and this document exists so it can link to one
place instead of reading Tyto's own architecture notes.

Tyto never knows about Jira, Drive, OAuth or machine identity. It is handed a folder and
writes a folder.

## The task folder

```
<task>/
  brief.brief          written by the caller (or by a person)
  assets/              the issue's attachments; paths in the brief resolve against it
  out/                 written by Tyto
    <artwork>-<format>.png|jpg|webp|svg
    result.json
```

`assets/` is optional. When it is absent, relative asset paths in the brief resolve
against the task folder itself.

## Invocation

```
tyto render <task>/brief.brief --out <task>/out
```

`--out` **is** the output folder: Tyto writes into exactly the directory named, and creates
it if it is not there. Useful flags for a caller: `--types png,jpeg,webp,svg` (defaults to
`png`), `--scale`, `--quality`, `--template`, `--formats`, `--json`. `tyto render --help`
is authoritative.

**`--template` and `--formats` are fallbacks, not overrides.** Each applies only when the
brief's frontmatter says nothing on that subject, so what the brief says about itself always
wins over what one invocation says about the brief. A caller that needs to force a template
writes it into the frontmatter.

## Exit codes

| Code | Means | Detail | Worth retrying |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | ok | Nothing went wrong. `result.json` has `status: "ok"`. | no |
| `1` | error diagnostics | The brief, the template or a frame produced an error — or the command line was refused. `result.json` has `status: "error"` and lists what went wrong, except when the command line was refused, in which case no run started and no `result.json` was written. | no |
| `2` | internal failure | Something threw that is not about this brief: a browser that will not launch, an unwritable output folder. `result.json` may be absent. | **yes** |

**Only `2` is worth retrying.** That is the whole reason there are two non-zero codes: a
brief that does not compile will not compile on the second attempt either, and a caller that
retried both would either loop forever or give up on a transient failure.

## `result.json`

The only file a caller has to read. It is written **last**, after every artifact it lists,
and atomically — so its appearance is the signal that the task is finished, and a reader
never sees it naming a file that is not there yet.

| Field | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Did anything go wrong, and nothing else. **Not** "did everything finish" — a run the caller cancelled is `ok` with fewer artifacts, because nothing went wrong. Derived from the diagnostics, so it cannot say `ok` over a page of errors. |
| `cancelled` | The caller stopped the run before the last frame was written. |
| `planned` | Artworks × formats × encodings the run set out to produce, counted before anything was rendered. Compare it with `artifacts.length` to tell a cancelled run from a complete one. |
| `artifacts` | One entry per file actually written, in scene order — artwork, then format, then the order the encodings were asked for. `bytes` is the size on disk, so a zero-byte file is distinguishable from a real render. |
| `diagnostics` | Every error and warning the run produced, from every stage. `range` is a pair of offsets into a source file; which file is not carried here (see *What this does not say*). |
| `tyto` | Which Tyto, and which templates at which versions, produced this — what makes a run reproducible. |

The machine-readable schema is **[`render-result.schema.json`](./render-result.schema.json)**,
generated from the same Zod schema that validates the document before Tyto writes it.

## Versioning

The schema file is the artefact to diff. What counts as a break:

- **Breaking:** removing a field, renaming one, narrowing a type, or adding a value to
  `status`. Also **adding any field** — the schema is `additionalProperties: false`, so a
  consumer validating strictly rejects a document with a field it has not been told about.
  That is deliberate: a strict schema turns a silent mismatch into a loud one, and the cost
  is that growth is a versioned event rather than a surprise.
- **Not breaking:** a new diagnostic code, a new artifact `kind` in an existing run, more
  entries in an existing array.

A breaking change ships as a major version of `@tyto/io` and a note in this document.
Pre-1.0, that is a minor (`docs/git-workflow.md`).

## What this does not say

- **Which file a diagnostic's `range` points into.** A render produces diagnostics about the
  brief and about the template in one flat list, and `Diagnostic` carries no provenance. The
  CLI knows, because it composes both, and prints `path:line:col` on stderr — but
  `result.json` carries offsets alone. A consumer that needs the file has to use the
  human-readable output or wait for provenance on the diagnostic itself.
- **Anything about `inbox/` or `outbox/`.** `tyto watch` is a convenience for a person and
  a simulator for this contract; a caller driving Tyto directly uses `tyto render`.
- **Whether a template exists.** The caller chooses the template and writes it into the
  frontmatter; Tyto validates it against the manifests it can see and answers
  `E_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE` when it cannot. There is no template catalogue outside
  `templates/*/manifest.yaml`.
